findings.problem: Both tests read the live SOURCETEXTS readings.json and find the four Kedushah parts by segment corresp. The planned data edit turns those corresp values into canonical. After it, validate_redirection raises 'Redirection needs one source segment per identity', and the library fixture ends up with no segments, so validate_pure_parts raises 'require identified words'. So the preflight only works before the edit and turns CI red on the edit commit. Neither test protects anything afterwards.
findings.required_fix: Before committing any data edit, either run both tests against a frozen copy of the pre-edit data (a fixture next to marmorstein_accepted_660.json) or make them handle both states. Before the edit they would find parts by corresp. After it they would find canonical segments, apply the same no-controls and no-interpretation checks to them, check that the shared-parts library has byte-identical fragments, and check the T2 output order on the real edited unit.

findings.location: validate_occurrences.check_order; build.require_review by_identity (still open from previous finding 9)
findings.problem: Only {'unit': <pure stem>} is rejected at the data stage. These are not rejected: an order 'reference', a segment 'transclude' or 'repeat', or a repeat_cue target naming the pure unit urn or one of its part identities. validate_redirection does not look for incoming segment 'transclude' or order 'reference' targets either. Also, require_review builds by_identity from raw units with map_root defaulting to True, and the raw pure unit has no map_root key. So a documentary transclude of the pure urn passes the review check, even though the generated pure file emits no corresp for that urn.
findings.required_fix: Reject any reference, transclude, repeat or repeat_cue target equal to the pure urn. Decide explicitly whether a single-part reference to a pure identity is allowed. If it is, document it as a canonical caller. If not, reject it. Exclude canonical_parts units from by_identity. Add those targets to validate_redirection's scan of incoming references. Test each case.

findings.problem: touches() only strips '@'. A spine reference written as a range string (START-END in target, with no targetEnd), which build.py passes through unchanged, is never in the identity set. It returns False, so a range covering a corrected identity skips the source_witness requirement. validate_generated already parses ranges with split_range, but this guard does not.
findings.required_fix: Normalize target and endpoint with opensiddur.exporter.urn.split_range before calling touches, and do the same for reuse, repeat and transclude values. Add a test where expanded_order has {'reference': {'target': P+'/before-/part'}} and no source_witness, which must raise.

findings.problem: The build checks the baseline only when readings.json names it or a canonical_parts unit exists. Edits for Kavod, Pachdekha or the Kedushah redirect that come before the library is added would only be gated by the unit test, not by the build.
findings.required_fix: In the first data-edit commit, add 'accepted_literal_baseline' to readings.json. Preferably also make the build require it whenever any unit has canonical_home, canonical or page_context.

findings.problem: With inline_scope and a half-verse part, the part branch forbids chapter_corresp and source_reference_corresp, and inline mode drops n. The opening chapter and verse milestones inside the seg then have neither n nor corresp. Under JLPTEI-3 rule 3 they are only terminators and open nothing. The old mode has the same meaning (with n, they are still terminators), so this is not a regression. But it is noise and untested, and the n-less form cannot be told apart from the closing terminators. Nothing tests that a non-boolean inline_scope is rejected.
findings.required_fix: Reject inline_scope together with source_reference_part, or leave out the bare chapter and verse openers in that case. Add tests for that combination and for inline_scope='yes' raising 'explicitly boolean'.

findings.location: importer spec line 68; JLPTEI-3 'Prefer milestones' (lines 217-219) and the verse/@n table (line 287)
findings.problem: The importer spec allows milestones inside seg type='quotation', but JLPTEI-3 still says to put the correspondence milestone before the semantic span. Neither document records that n is omitted. The stated reason ('not printed source labels') does not match JLPTEI-3: there, verse/@n is the canonical number, and display is controlled by the opensiddur:verse-numbering setting. The importer spec also says not to change encoding to hide a rendering problem.
findings.required_fix: Record the n omission and its exact scope (inline_scope only; corresp is always kept) next to line 68. Get the processor owner to confirm, or cross-reference the exception from JLPTEI-3. Check in the PDF/HTML outputs that verse-numbering behaves correctly with milestones that have no n.

previous_findings_closed: 1 (high) literal-context page_start default: prepare_documents now counts a break only when the scan changes and page_start is not False (realizations.py:352-356). New test 'same_scan_default' covers it.

2 (medium) pure-parts identity: prepare_unit forces map_root=False and omit_publication_urn=True. validate_generated rejects any idno or div@corresp in the pure file, and there is a per-project check for duplicate publication URNs. Tests cover 'publication' and 'root'. The pure unit's urn is never emitted.

3 (medium) circular literal pb check: the expected list is now built from raw fragments (scan change plus page_start → n, facs, text before the break) and compared with the generated pb n, facs and text before it. Tests cover remove, inject and move.

4 (medium) negative tests on generated output: home_pb, context_identity, context_other_identity, missing/duplicate idno and duplicate_publication, plus pure-file pb, note, head, conditional, declare, transclude, root, publication, targetEnd and range-string targets, are all tested.
5 (medium) correction overlap: the overlap check now covers the whole before+sic+after span. Tests cover before and after against both alternative and optional overlays.
6 (low) ambiguous locator: there are separate tests for 0 and 2 matches, each checking the exact 'Correction has_hast: N places match' message.

7 (medium) R12/T10: an unbound literal correction applies next to a bound home correction. A literal file that emits P/part is rejected with 'one generated home'. Resolved, literal and corrected sha256 values are checked against the actual texts.

8 (low) attester bypass: reuse, repeat and transclude pointing at a corrected identity are rejected. Spine references must name a source_witness from the attester set. Payloads include sha256 of both order lists plus documentary_instructions and navigation. One gap remains for range-string targets (see findings).

10 (low) context_urn: mitigated rather than removed. The fallback to the unit urn stays, but it only passes for units whose urn contains ':siddur:' (the two existing contexts). Context div@corresp is now checked against the global canonical set, and duplicate idno checks make context URNs unique. The diff confirms that the only change to the two existing contexts is that corresp moves to the wrapper div.
11 (low) invalid-target test: the require_review assertion that passed for the wrong reason is gone. A separate test now shows that a valid remap changes the occurrence receipt.
missing_design_requirements: R2: validate_redirection does not look for incoming segment 'transclude' or order 'reference' targets, and it runs only as a test before the edit (findings 1 and 2).
T2 remainder: no assertion that the non-redirected Kedushah parts keep their corresp, and the real-data T2 test will break after the edit (finding 1).
Not code gaps: T6 (each of the five hosts passes the line-232 guard) and R12 for real units 119/203 can only be shown with real edited data (see integration_checks).
